subject: Cross-border evidence request: data handover & processing layers
messages:
From: Susan Carter <susan.carter@asterbio.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@asterbio.com>, legal@asterbio.com
Date: 2028-10-10 09:12 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence for cross-border data handover and processing layers

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at AsterBio liked the routing controls you showed. Procurement and Legal asked me to follow up with a concise evidence pack for our data export assessment. Specifically we need: 

- A DPF-style mapping describing where customer data may traverse or be processed (EU controllers -> processor paths, any US or APAC execution).
- The proposed DPA annex (redlines are fine) and confirmation of SCCs/appropriate transfer mechanisms.
- KMS/Key custody description (who holds keys, HSM/KMS provider, split-key policy if any).
- Operational evidence for log retention and audit trails (sample schema or log extract stub is fine).
- Any model-routing/kv-cache considerations that could cause cross-border transients.

Can you send an initial packet (PDF/attachments or Drive links) by EOD PT on 10/13? We may need to share with our EU data protection officer.

Also, please include an estimated timeline if any DPA negotiation will require an SLA exception.

Best,
Susan
Susan Carter
Head of Procurement, AsterBio

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Carter <susan.carter@asterbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-10 11:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for cross-border data handover and processing layers

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching an initial evidence packet inline and linking a Drive folder for full artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDRIVE-DPF-EVIDENCE (read-only).

What I attached: redwood_dpf_summary.pdf (overview mapping + narrative), dpa_annex_v1.2.docx (working draft with placeholders for your counsel), sccs_mapping.xlsx (matrix mapping SCCs to processing activities), kms-keyflow-diagram.png (key custody flow).

Quick answers up front:
- Transfer mechanism: we support standard SCCs today; if you need EU Commission adequacy alternatives (e.g., DPF+contractual clauses), we can include an addendum.
- KMS: Customer data at rest is encrypted with per-tenant keys by default in our managed KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS depending on region). For Private deployments we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM-backed key material and limited Redwood-admin access.
- Logs: audit logs (control-plane) and request-level traces are retained per our retention schedule — the Drive folder contains a redacted sample log extract and the log-schema doc.
- Model routing / KV cache: we use region-aware routing policies. Default behavior pins inference to a region; KV cache lifecycles are tied to the serving instance and not replicated across regions unless the customer explicitly enables multi-region replication.

Next steps: 1) I looped in Ben, Karthik and Kimberly to finalize KMS and DPA-side language; 2) We can jump on a 30-min call with your DPO and legal on 10/12 or 10/13. What works?

Att: redwood_dpf_summary.pdf, dpa_annex_v1.2.docx, sccs_mapping.xlsx, kms-keyflow-diagram.png

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-10-11 08:30 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Quick tasks for AsterBio packet (deadline EOD 10/12)

Team — please see Susan's request and the packet I sent. Action items below (deadline EOD PT 10/12 so we can hit client EOD 10/13):

- Ben: can you provide the redacted control-plane audit log sample and a short note on retention SLA (where stored, retention periods, access controls)? Put the sample in the Drive folder and add a one-paragraph explanation.
- Karthik: can you confirm the exact wording we should use for the DPA annex regarding "onward transfers" and whether we can include an explicit DPF statement mapping runtime routing layers (model routing / cache / batch workers)? Recommend a short clause (2-3 bullets) we can include in v1.2.
- Kimberly: can you produce the KMS/BYOK implementation note — include supported providers, rotation cadence, HSM usage, and the limited-access policy for Redwood ops. If there's a SOC-2 control reference, call it out.

I'll assemble updated artifacts and aim to send everything to Susan by EOD 10/13. If anyone needs redlines directly in the dpa_annex_v1.2.docx, drop them in comments on the Drive doc.

Thanks — Aisha

From: Susan Carter <susan.carter@asterbio.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@asterbio.com>
Date: 2028-10-12 10:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for cross-border data handover and processing layers

Thanks Aisha, the initial packet is helpful. A few clarifying questions before we circulate to our DPO: 

1) For the KMS/BYOK flow — can you confirm whether customer-managed keys can be used to encrypt KV cache material (not just persistent storage)? If not, we need to understand the threat model.
2) In sccs_mapping.xlsx there are entries for "model evaluation" and "inference runtime" — are those ever executed outside the EU by default? We need explicit confirmation that inference for EU controllers is routed to EU-only capacity unless the customer configures cross-region routing.
3) The DPA annex mentions "onward transfers per policy" — can you provide a short paragraph that reads well for contract language: who is the onward transferee, where data may go, and our fallback (e.g., replicate to US for capacity / disaster recovery only with notice).

If you can add these clarifications and an updated DPA annex with the paragraph, we should be able to progress quickly. Also, can you include a short sample audit log showing an access event with timestamp, actor (redacted), action, and region? The redacted sample you included is useful but missing the actor field.

Best,
Susan

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Carter <susan.carter@asterbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-13 16:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for cross-border data handover and processing layers

Susan — thanks for the follow-ups. Attached are the updated artifacts and a short, contract-ready paragraph for the DPA annex (see dpa_annex_v1.2.docx, now v1.3 in Drive). Highlights below and attachments in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDRIVE-DPF-EVIDENCE

1) KV cache & BYOK: Customer-managed keys (BYOK) can be used for persistent at-rest encryption only. KV cache (ephemeral in-memory and local disk caches tied to serving instances) is encrypted at rest using tenant-scoped keys in the serving region; we do not currently support BYOK for ephemeral cache material. Threat model: ephemeral cache lifecycles are short (<72h default), are region-bound by default, and access to key material for cache encryption is restricted to the serving instance with no human-readable exports. For customers requiring BYOK at the cache-layer we offer Private deployment options where the entire serving stack can be placed under customer-controlled keys/HSM.

2) Region routing: By default, inference requests are routed to region-specific pools. For EU controllers, inference is pinned to EU capacity unless cross-region routing is explicitly enabled in the tenant configuration or via traffic rules. We included a short operational note in the DPA annex: "Redwood will process EU-controller data in EU-hosted compute unless the customer explicitly authorises cross-region processing in writing."

3) Onward transfers paragraph (contract-ready):
"Onward transfers: Where Redwood engages third-party subprocessors or routes requests to neighbouring compute regions to satisfy customer-configured routing, Redwood will ensure that such transfers are governed by appropriate safeguards (EU Standard Contractual Clauses or other lawful transfer mechanisms). Transfers for disaster recovery or capacity overflow will only occur under predefined escalation procedures; Redwood will provide prior notice where feasible and a summary post-event report. Customer may opt for Private deployment to avoid cross-border replication."

4) Audit log sample: added a redacted log line with actor-type (service-account), timestamp, action, and region. See attached file sample_audit_event_redacted.log (in Drive).

Next steps: I uploaded v1.3 of the DPA annex and the supplemental KMS note and log sample. If that reads clean to your counsel, I've added a DocuSign envelope for the DPA annex here: https://www.docusign.com/sign/EXAMPLE_DPA_ANNEX (expires 2028-11-01). We can also schedule a 30-min follow-up with your DPO on 10/16.

Thanks — look forward to next steps.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
